analysis:
The only changed file is a Swift test file, DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift. The change parameterizes the fixture() helper with an optional artifact digest and adds or adjusts planner tests: assistant quote handling, widening-quote steering, credit-refusal bookkeeping, and strict decoding of the saved assistant configuration. The test code uses constructed profiles, fixture hosts (192.0.2.x) and a temporary home directory created with mode 0700 and cleaned up in deinit. It contains no secrets, no network calls and no production code paths.

The tests exercise security-relevant planner behavior. ClusterConfigurationCodec rejects a null tensorAssistant, wrong types, an uppercase inventory hash, extra keys and duplicate keys. ClusterAutomaticSetupHandoff.requireCompatible refuses a dropped or changed assistant policy. Link probe history is ignored when it is foreign, stale, malformed or world-readable. These checks strengthen test coverage and do not weaken any control.

I found no regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumption. This review saw only the test file, and the patch excerpt is truncated. I did not see the production planner, codec and handoff implementations that these tests assert against, and they are outside the supplied evidence. Nothing here touches TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or the T-041 prefix-cache surfaces.
